questions.problem: Suppose that $|\,p\,|=8$, $|\,q\,|=4$ and that the angle between the vectors is $\theta =\frac{\pi }{4}.$ Find the vector projection of $p$ onto $q$ in terms of the vector $q.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the scalar projection as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{q}\,p & =|\,p\,|\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =8\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =8\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & =4\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the unit vector that is parallel to $q:$

$$
u=\frac{q}{|\,q\,|}=\frac{q}{4}=\frac{1}{4}q
$$

Finally, we compute the vector projection as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,p & ={\text{comp}}_{q}\,p\cdot u \\  & =4\sqrt{2}\cdot \frac{1}{4}q \\  & =\sqrt{2}q\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Suppose that $|\,a\,|=36$, $|\,b\,|=6$ and that the angle between the vectors is $\theta ={135}^{∘}.$ Find the vector projection of $a$ onto $b$ in terms of the vector $b.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the scalar projection as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{b}\,a & =|\,a\,|\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =36\operatorname{cos}⁡({135}^{∘}) \\  & =36\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\  & =-18\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the unit vector that is parallel to $b:$

$$
u=\frac{b}{|\,b\,|}=\frac{b}{6}=\frac{1}{6}b
$$

Finally, we compute the vector projection as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,a & ={\text{comp}}_{b}\,a\cdot u \\  & =(-18\sqrt{2})\cdot \frac{1}{6}b \\  & =-3\sqrt{2}b\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the scalar projection as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{d}\,c & =|\,c\,|\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =10\operatorname{cos}⁡({30}^{∘}) \\  & =10\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\  & =5\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{d}\,c & ={\text{comp}}_{d}\,c\cdot u \\  & =5\sqrt{3}\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{3}}d \\  & =\frac{5}{2}d\end{aligned}

questions.problem: Let $a=⟨0,-3,1⟩$ and $b=⟨\sqrt{2},1,0⟩.$ Find the vector projection of $a$ onto $b.$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{a\cdot b}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{0\cdot \sqrt{2}+(-3)\cdot 1+1\cdot 0}{(\sqrt{2})^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{-3}{3}⟨\sqrt{2},1,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-\sqrt{2},-1,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Let $a=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 3 \\ 3\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}]$ and $b=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$ Find the vector projection of $b$ onto $a.$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{a}\,b & =\frac{a\cdot b}{a\cdot a}a \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{{a}_{x}^{2}+{a}_{y}^{2}+{a}_{z}^{2}}a \\  & =\frac{6\cdot 3+3\cdot 1+3\sqrt{2}\cdot 0}{{6}^{2}+{3}^{2}+(3\sqrt{2})^{2}}a \\  & =\frac{21}{63}⟨6,3,3\sqrt{2}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨6,3,3\sqrt{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨2,1,\sqrt{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{v}\,u & =\frac{u\cdot v}{v\cdot v}v \\  & =\frac{{u}_{x}{v}_{x}+{u}_{y}{v}_{y}+{u}_{z}{v}_{z}}{{v}_{x}^{2}+{v}_{y}^{2}+{v}_{z}^{2}}v \\  & =\frac{(1)\cdot 2+(-2)\cdot 1+(1)\cdot 0}{{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}}v \\  & =\frac{0}{5}v \\  & =⟨\,0,0,0\,⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we must have

$$
r⊥s\,⟹\,r\cdot s=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot s & ={r}_{x}\cdot {s}_{x}+{r}_{y}\cdot {s}_{y}+{r}_{z}\cdot {s}_{z} \\  & =(-5)\cdot n+1\cdot (-2)+3\cdot 4 \\  & =-5n-2+12 \\  & =10-5n.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot s & =0 \\ 10-5n & =0 \\ n & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Let $a=⟨-5,-3,1⟩$ and $b=⟨x,-2,-3⟩.$ Given that the projection of $a$ onto $b$ is the zero vector, find the value of $x.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $a$ is a nonzero vector, its projection onto another nonzero vector $b$ equals the zero vector only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
a⊥b\,⟹\,a\cdot b=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & ={a}_{x}\cdot {b}_{x}+{a}_{y}\cdot {b}_{y}+{a}_{z}\cdot {b}_{z} \\  & =-5\cdot x+(-3)\cdot (-2)+1\cdot (-3) \\  & =3-5x.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & =0 \\ 3-5x & =0 \\ -5x & =-3 \\ x & =\frac{3}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Suppose that $|\,\mathbf{a}\,|=8,|\,\mathbf{b}\,|=4$ and that the angle between the vectors is $\theta = \dfrac{5\pi}{6}.$ Find the vector projection of $\mathbf{a}$ onto $\mathbf{b}$ in terms of the vector $\mathbf{b}.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we find the scalar projection as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{b}\,a & =|\,a\,|\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =8\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{6}) \\  & =8\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\  & =-4\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the unit vector that is parallel to $\mathbf{b}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\mathbf{u} = \dfrac{\mathbf{b}}{|\,\mathbf{b}\,|} = \dfrac{\mathbf{b}}{4} = \dfrac{1}{4} \mathbf{b}
$$

Finally, we compute the vector projection as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,a & ={\text{comp}}_{b}\,a\cdot u \\  & =-4\sqrt{3}\cdot \frac{1}{4}b \\  & =-\sqrt{3}b\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Let $\mathbf{a}=\langle 1,-3,5 \rangle$ and $\mathbf{b}=\langle 5,-4,0 \rangle$. Find the vector projection of $\mathbf{a}$ onto $\mathbf{b}$.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{a\cdot b}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{1\cdot 5+(-3)\cdot (-4)+5\cdot 0}{{5}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+{0}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{17}{41}⟨5,-4,0⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{85}{41},-\frac{68}{41},0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Let $[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ and $[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$. Find the vector projection of $\mathbf{a}$ onto $\mathbf{b}$.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{a\cdot b}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{1\cdot 1+0\cdot 5+1\cdot (-1)}{{1}^{2}+{5}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{0}{{1}^{2}+{5}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}b \\  & =⟨0,0,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
